status: CALIBRATION: internal only, no live writer, customer publication off
purpose: Tonight's moon phase, illumination, moonrise/moonset, sunset/sunrise and civil/nautical/astronomical twilight for every registry.lakes lake, plus the on-water darkness class. Path /lakes/{k}/states/moon (Publisher declaration: moon-publication-v1.json).

night.definition: Tonight for calendar date D = the night starting on the evening of D at the lake. Span = [D 12:00 UTC - lon/15 h, +24 h): local solar noon to local solar noon, so every longitude gets exactly one evening and the following morning. All instants are UTC (ISO 8601 Z); the client renders them in the lake's zone.
night.fishingWindow: Mirrors the Engine and iOS (ConditionsInputBuilder; iOS specs/conditions-engine.md 'the night window runs into TOMORROW'): start = astronomical dusk, else sunset + 80 min; end = the next sunrise, else start + 8 h. Basis values: ASTRONOMICAL_DUSK_TO_SUNRISE, SUNSET_PLUS_80_MIN_TO_SUNRISE, (either)_FALLBACK_8H, POLAR_NIGHT_WHOLE_SPAN, NO_NIGHT_SUN_ALWAYS_UP.
night.illuminationInstant: Moon illumination, phase fraction and phase name are evaluated at local solar midnight (span start + 12 h). This differs from the app's request-instant value: see divergences.
night.defaultDate: Without an explicit date, each lake gets its own tonight: the night whose span contains the run, or the coming evening once that night's sunrise has passed (night.evening_date). Never the UTC date.

algorithms.ephemeris: sector-moon-v1 (contracts/moon/moon-v1.json): Paul Schlyter's low-precision Sun and Moon positions, ported line for line from Sources/SectorEngine/Engine/Astronomy.swift. Illumination, phaseFraction and phaseName pass the spec's 52 vectors (tolerance 0.0005 / 1e-6).
algorithms.siderealTime: IAU 1982 GMST (Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms 2nd ed., eq. 12.4).
algorithms.events: Meeus ch. 15 / USNO standard altitudes. Sun rise/set: centre at -0.8333 deg. Civil, nautical, astronomical twilight: centre at -6, -12, -18 deg. Moon rise/set: upper limb on the horizon with 34' refraction, geocentric altitude of the centre h0 = 0.7275 * horizontal parallax - 0.5667 deg. Altitude sampled every 10 min and bisected to 1 s; positions recomputed at every trial instant.
algorithms.moonlight: presence = mean of max(0, sin(topocentric moon altitude)) sampled every 15 min across the fishing window, end inclusive (the Engine's moonAltitudeFraction). upFraction = share of samples with the moon's centre above the horizon.
algorithms.absentEvents: An event that does not occur in the span (polar day or night, a moon that does not rise or set) is null, and sunState says why (ALWAYS_ABOVE / ALWAYS_BELOW). It is never interpolated.

usnoCrossCheck.reference: brains/moon/tests/fixtures/usno_reference.json (USNO Astronomical Applications API rstt/oneday, moon/phases and the yearly twilight tables, retrieved 2026-11-22)

weatherInput.producer: Weather Brain (brainId weather; Engine PR #234), document /lakes/{k}/states/weather
weatherInput.status: The Weather Brain is not on main yet, so the input is not declared in brain.json consumes; add {kind: brain, brainId: weather} when it lands. Until then run.py --weather passes {lakeId: Weather state document}.
read: forecast.hourly[].{at, cloudCoverPct}: the NWS forecast grid, the next 12 hours after the Weather run (origin forecastGrid)
sky.cloudCoverPct {value, at, origin}: the current hour (forecast grid, or the observation's cloud layers when the grid has no hour)
weatherInput.notRead: Every other Weather field. Only these cloud rows enter the input fingerprint, so an unrelated Weather change does not trigger a recompute.
weatherInput.use: Each row is keyed on the top of its hour. The window's hours are the top-of-hour instants within [window start - 30 min, window end + 30 min]. At least 75 % of those DISTINCT hours need a value; the cloud is their mean. A repeated hour with the same value counts once; with different values the input is refused. A null value is skipped. Because the forecast reaches 12 hours ahead, only a Weather state generated close to dusk covers a whole night.
weatherInput.whenMissing: status MISSING with a reason: NO_WEATHER_INPUT, UNSUPPORTED_WEATHER_INPUT (not a sector-brain-weather-state-v1 document), NO_HOURLY_CLOUD_COVER, MALFORMED_HOURLY_ROW (missing field, or a timestamp without an explicit UTC offset), CLOUD_COVER_OUT_OF_RANGE, CONFLICTING_HOURLY_VALUES, INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE. No cloud value is assumed.

divergences.note: Where this Brain deliberately differs from other sector-moon-v1 consumers and the app's Darkness tile. Read before comparing numbers.
divergences.illuminationInstant: The Brain evaluates illumination, phase fraction and phase name at local solar midnight of tonight's span. The Engine /conditions moonIllumination and the app's Moon tile use the request instant (the Moon sheet's chart samples about 9 PM). The same night can differ by a few percentage points (about 3 points per 6 h near the quarters), and the phase NAME can flip near a band edge. Both come from the same sector-moon-v1 math.
divergences.cityGlow: The cloud cancel uses the Engine's DEFAULT city glow 0.3 for every lake. The app's Darkness factor uses the per-request cityGlow when one is supplied. At a spot with a different glow value the same cloud cancels a different share (rural 1.0 vs 0.76 here vs 0.2 in a city), so the class can differ from the app's label.
divergences.cloudBasis: The Brain uses the mean cloud cover over the fishing window from the Weather Brain. The Engine uses the current cloud cover and treats a missing value as 0 %. The Brain treats a missing value as MOON_ONLY.
divergences.eventTimes: Rise, set and twilight use the USNO standard altitudes inside a noon-to-noon span. The Engine's Astronomy.moonRiseSet uses the moon's centre at 0 deg within the UTC day (see docs/brains/MOON_BRAIN_PLAN.md section 2).

darknessRule.statedBeforeScoring: 2026-11-22. Constants are the Engine's DarknessFactor and ConditionsConfig.Darkness, so the Brain and the app classify the same night the same way.

inputs.I: moon illumination at local solar midnight (0..1)
inputs.P: moon presence across the fishing window (0..1)
inputs.cloudPct: window mean cloud cover from weatherInput, when AVAILABLE

darknessRule.cloudCancel: C = clamp((cloudPct - 50) / 50, 0, 1) * (1 - 0.8 * 0.3). 0.3 is the Engine's default city-glow factor: no per-lake skyglow input exists, so the rule uses the Engine's constant, not a per-lake estimate.

classes.when: the Sun does not set in the span

basis.MOON_AND_CLOUD: cloud cover AVAILABLE: A uses C.
basis.MOON_ONLY: cloud cover MISSING: A = I * P, the clear-sky upper bound on moonlight. The state says so in `statement` and names the reason. Unlike the Engine (cloud ?? 0), nothing is assumed.

darknessRule.alwaysReported: moonOnly {moonlightIndex, class, label} is reported on every night, cloud or not.
darknessRule.notClaimed: The class describes moonlight competing with the boat's lights (shooter visibility). It makes no claim that a bright moon makes fish hold deeper or spook (iOS specs/weather-metric-detail.md 'Copy accuracy (moon)'). Artificial skyglow is not modelled. Not validated against measured on-water light.
